en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.fingers.name: Finger counting
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.fingers.desc: A line-art hand marks the next fingertip or finger joint on each count — a visual aid for the Sunnah way of counting.
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.geometric.name: Geometric rosette
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.geometric.desc: A twelve-point star inside a ring of 33 petals. Each count fills one petal; 99 completes the rosette three times.
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.stars.name: Night sky
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.stars.desc: Each count lights one star of a constellation that completes at the end of the round.
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.pebbles.name: Date pits / pebbles
en.tasbeehDesigns.designs.pebbles.desc: Each count moves one date pit or pebble from one dish to the other. The note explains the evidence and how scholars grade it.
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.title: About this design
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.pebbles.body: A report tells of a woman who counted her tasbeeh on date pits or pebbles in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ; he taught her a fuller wording and is not reported to have objected. Scholars grade this report differently. Many allow counting with pebbles, date pits or beads, while others hold that counting on the fingertips is better. Every design counts exactly the same.
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.pebbles.tirmidhi3568: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3568 — hasan gharib (at-Tirmidhi), hasan (Bashar Awwad Ma'ruf), da'if (al-Albani), munkar (Ahmad Shakir)
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.pebbles.abudawud1500: Sunan Abu Dawud 1500 — hasan li-ghayrihi (Shu'aib al-Arna'ut), da'if (al-Albani)
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.fingers.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught counting zikr on the fingertips. This hand is only a visual aid — your own finger method is fine, whichever way you were taught to count. Every design counts exactly the same.
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.fingers.abudawud1501: Sunan Abu Dawud 1501 — counting on the fingertips: hasan (al-Albani, Shu'aib al-Arna'ut)
en.tasbeehDesigns.note.fingers.tirmidhi3583: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3583 — gradings differ: hasan (Ahmad Shakir), da'if (al-Albani)
